<https://fandaws.com/ontology/bfo/valuenet-core#TextualRepresentation> <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment> "Form, not content (D-005). CCO defines information content entity as equivalent to a generically dependent continuant that is about some entity: asserting that a representation is about something, through cco:is about or any subproperty such as designates or describes, re-classifies it as information content. <https://fandaws.com/ontology/bfo/valuenet-core#TextualRepresentation> <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment> "A changed string is a different TextualRepresentation. <https://fandaws.com/ontology/bfo/valuenet-core#TextualRepresentation> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A generically dependent continuant that is one exact sequence of Unicode code points and that generically depends on at least one information bearing entity."@en

added.triple: <https://fandaws.com/ontology/bfo/valuenet-core#TextSpan> <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment> "Individuated by position, not by its string (D-005): the same substring at two positions of one representation is two spans with the same hasTextualSequenceValue, and every selector of one span must give the same offsets. Not a subclass of TextualRepresentation, and not an evidence source by classification: it is evidence when an isEvidenceFor assertion or a ValueEvidenceAnnotation says so. Disjoint with information content entity (D-011): a span may be designated by a selector, but a span that is asserted to be about or to designate something makes the data inconsistent."@en

<https://fandaws.com/ontology/bfo/valuenet-core#TextualRepresentation> <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment> "Form, not content (D-005). CCO subtypes information content entities by what they are about; a representation is individuated by its exact sequence, a level CCO's information model has no class for, so it is placed directly under BFO generically dependent continuant. CCO defines information content entity as equivalent to a generically dependent continuant that is about some entity, and this class is disjoint with information content entity (D-011): asserting that a representation is about something, through cco:is about or any subproperty such as designates or describes, makes the data inconsistent. Relate a representation to what it expresses through a content-level information content entity instead."@en

<https://fandaws.com/ontology/bfo/valuenet-folk#FaithDisposition> <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment> "Differs from TrustDisposition, a firm belief in the reliability of someone or something, in not resting on evidence of that reliability. <https://fandaws.com/ontology/bfo/valuenet-folk#FaithDisposition> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A personal value disposition to place complete trust or confidence in someone or something without requiring proof."@en

<https://fandaws.com/ontology/bfo/valuenet-folk#FaithDisposition> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#example> "Staying confident that an estranged friend will make amends, and keeping a place for them, though nothing yet suggests they will."@en

<https://fandaws.com/ontology/bfo/valuenet-folk#OpennessDisposition> <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment> "Receptive rather than seeking: VarietyDisposition and AdventureDisposition seek out change and daring experience, OpenMindednessDisposition is receptive to ideas and opinions, and this class to experience. The definition formerly also covered being transparent and candid (R17, D-012); those senses are CandorDisposition and TransparencyDisposition, under HonestyDisposition. The broader conceptual matches below, Stimulation and Self-Direction, were already those of the sense kept."@en

<https://fandaws.com/ontology/bfo/valuenet-folk#OpennessDisposition> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A personal value disposition to be receptive to new experiences, including unfamiliar activities, sensations, and ways of living."@en

<https://fandaws.com/ontology/bfo/valuenet-folk#OpennessDisposition> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#example> "Accepting an invitation to a festival of a culture one knows nothing about, and taking part rather than watching."@en

<https://fandaws.com/ontology/bfo/valuenet-folk#ReligionDisposition> <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment> "The religious sense formerly joined to FaithDisposition's definition (R17, D-012), and the class for folk:Religion in the folk corpus, which places it under Beliefs alongside Faith and Belief in God. <https://fandaws.com/ontology/bfo/valuenet-folk#ReligionDisposition> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#example> "Keeping the prayer and dietary observances of one's tradition, and weighing a major decision against its teaching."@en

archive.defect: dul:hasDataValue objects are relative IRI references rather than literals, and the property is declared owl:DataTypeProperty, which is not an OWL term. Both are the FRED export's behaviour, not damage to this copy.
archive.detection:
python -c "import zipfile,rdflib;z=zipfile.ZipFile('ThatsAllFolks/MFRC_1k_ESWC.zip');P=rdflib.URIRef('http://www.ontologydesignpatterns.org/ont/dul/DUL.owl#hasDataValue');m=o=d=0;
for n in z.namelist():
    t=z.read(n).decode('utf-8','replace') if n.endswith('.ttl') and not n.startswith('__MACOSX') else None
    if t is None or 'hasDataValue' not in t: continue
    d+= 'owl:DataTypeProperty' in t
    g=rdflib.Graph()
    g.parse(data=t,format='turtle',publicID='https://probe.invalid/'+n)
    c=sum(1 for _ in g.triples((None,P,None)))
    m+=bool(c); o+=c
print('members_affected',m,'occurrences',o,'members_with_misdeclared_property',d)"
archive.disposition: permanent upstream debt; bytes preserved. Repacking would fork an unaudited binary that nothing reads.
archive.note: No runtime test opens this archive. Tests assert its sha256 over the bytes.
archive.why_excluded: discover() walks Turtle files in the working tree. Archive members are not files in the working tree, so no corpus measure has ever seen them.

why: The matrix measured the corpus at eol-hardened-v1 and is frozen: its content is a comparison of three checkouts of one commit, so re-running it against a later corpus would replace the experiment rather than repeat it. This ledger is what lets the successor baseline cite it without pretending the two describe the same corpus.
